portName: Port de la Santé, Villefranche-sur-Mer (tender landing)
seoTitle: Villefranche cruise port guide: tender, Nice, Monaco, Èze
seoDescription: Villefranche is a tender port: boats land at Port de la Santé, steps from the old town. Train to Nice 7–10 min, Monaco 15–20 min. Bus 600 €2.10 (2026).
quickAnswer: Villefranche is a tender port: ships anchor in the bay and tenders land at Port de la Santé, a few minutes' walk from the old town. Nice is 7–10 minutes and Monaco 15–20 minutes by train from Villefranche station, about 10 minutes' walk from the tender quay. Be back at the tender quay 90 minutes before all-aboard, and 120 minutes before if your day includes a train or bus.
intro: Villefranche-sur-Mer sits on a bay between Nice and Cap Ferrat, and big ships anchor offshore and send passengers ashore by tender. The landing, Port de la Santé, is a small harbour north of the citadel run directly by the Alpes-Maritimes departmental council, and it handles more than 200,000 cruise passengers a year. The old town, the Cocteau chapel and the citadel are all on foot from the quay; Nice and Monaco are short train rides. Since a prefectoral order of 9 December 2025, Villefranche takes only one ship of more than 1,300 passengers a day, an average of 2,000 cruise passengers a day (3,000 on some calls), and no more than 15 calls a month in July and August.
tenderNotes: Ships anchor in the bay and tenders land at Port de la Santé, at the western end of the village below the citadel. The tender ride takes about 10–15 minutes. The landing has a small terminal with a tourist information desk and toilets, and taxis wait outside. Queues for the tenders back to the ship can build in the afternoon, so return early.

terminals.name: Port de la Santé tender landing
terminals.notes: Small harbour north of the citadel, managed by the Alpes-Maritimes departmental council. The old town and waterfront are a few minutes' walk away, uphill in places. Villefranche station is about 600 m away, roughly 10 minutes on foot along the Promenade des Marinières, with stairs and a short climb. The Octroi bus stop (lines 15 and 600) is about 7 minutes' walk.

walkability.detail: The old town and harbour front are a few minutes from the tender landing, and the Rue Obscure is a few steps up from the port. The village is built on a slope, so expect stairs and steep lanes. The station and Plage des Marinières are about 10 minutes' walk.

transportSections.cost: Fare not confirmed for this guide; check SNCF TER before you travel
transportSections.detail: Walk about 10 minutes from the tender quay to Villefranche station, which is next to the Plage des Marinières. Trains on the Nice–Menton line run frequently. From Nice-Ville the old town is a 15–20 minute walk; from Monaco station the Casino area is about 10 minutes on foot.

transportSections.cost: €2.10 by contactless card, €2.50 cash to the driver (2026)
transportSections.time: Every 10–15 minutes on weekdays, every 20 minutes at weekends
transportSections.detail: Stops at Octroi in Villefranche, about 7 minutes' walk from the port. It runs along the coast to Nice and to Monaco and Menton. Lignes d'Azur tickets are accepted for Nice–Monaco trips that do not enter Monaco. Traffic on the coast road makes the bus less predictable than the train.
Runs from the Octroi stop to Nice in one direction and Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat in the other. Cheaper than the train but slower on busy cruise days.

Èze is about five miles from the pier. By public transport, bus 83 runs from Beaulieu-sur-Mer via Èze-sur-Mer station up to the village, and lines 82 and 602 run from Nice. Times were not confirmed for this guide, so a taxi or a ship tour is the safer choice on a short call. The last part of the village is reached by steps.

transportSections.time: About 15–20 min to Nice, 30–40 min to Monaco, depending on traffic
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait outside the tender terminal, and the village rank is on Place Amélie Pollonnais (+33 4 93 55 55 55). Availability can be short on busy days.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the tender quay at Port de la Santé 90 minutes before all-aboard if you stay in Villefranche. If your day includes a train or bus to Nice or Monaco, be back at the quay 120 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: Tender queues build in the afternoon. From Nice-Ville, take a train that leaves at least 140 minutes before all-aboard; from Monaco station, at least 150 minutes before. From Villefranche station, allow about 10 minutes on foot, with stairs, back to the quay.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If trains are disrupted, take a taxi straight to Port de la Santé, or bus 600 to the Octroi stop. If you will miss the last tender, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once.

excursionAdvice: Nice and Monaco are easy on your own by train, so neither needs a tour. A ship tour is worth it for Èze, where bus connections are awkward and the village sits high above the coast, and for combined Èze–Monaco or Saint-Paul-de-Vence days that are hard to time on public transport around tenders.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship anchors at 08:00, tenders start soon after, and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Tender ashore to Port de la Santé and walk up to the Citadelle Saint-Elme.
Walk down through the Rue Obscure to the harbour and the Chapelle Saint-Pierre, open from 09:30 Wednesday to Sunday.
Walk about 10 minutes to Villefranche station and take the train to Nice-Ville.
Walk to Nice old town and the seafront.
Walk back to Nice-Ville and take the train to Villefranche.
Walk back past the Plage des Marinières to the tender quay.
At the tender quay, 120 minutes before all-aboard because the day included a train and the ship is at anchor.

sights.name: Chapelle Saint-Pierre (Cocteau chapel)
sights.why: Fishermen's chapel on the harbour, decorated inside and out by Jean Cocteau in 1956–57 with scenes from the life of Saint Peter. Listed as a historic monument since 1996.
sights.tip: Open Wednesday to Sunday, 09:30–12:30 and 14:00–18:00; closed Monday, Tuesday and from mid-November to mid-December.

sights.name: Citadelle Saint-Elme
sights.why: Citadel above the tender landing, with the Volti museum and gardens.
sights.tip: It is right by the tender quay, so it is an easy first or last stop.

sights.name: Rue Obscure
sights.why: A covered, arcaded street about 130 m long, built in 1260, a few steps up from the port.
sights.tip: Combine it with the walk from the citadel down to the harbour.

sights.name: Old harbour and Quai Courbet
sights.why: The waterfront of fishing boats, cafés and restaurants below the old town.
sights.tip: The harbour restaurants are good but expensive; cheaper places are on rue du Poilu.

sights.name: Nice old town and seafront
sights.why: The city next door, 7–10 minutes away by train.
sights.tip: From Nice-Ville station the old town is a 15–20 minute walk.

sights.name: Monaco
sights.why: The principality, 15–20 minutes by train, with the Casino area about 10 minutes' walk from the station.
sights.tip: Allow for the 10-minute walk from the Casino area back to the station when you plan the return.

sights.name: Exotic Garden of Èze
sights.why: Garden at the top of the hill village of Èze, about 10 km from Nice.
sights.tip: Open 09:00–18:30 in October and 09:00–16:30 in November and December. Access is by steps.

beaches.name: Plage des Marinières
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk about 10 minutes from the tender quay towards the station
beaches.note: Shallow drop-off and gravelly sand; suits families.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the return to the last tender.
commonMistakes.fix: Afternoon queues build at Port de la Santé. Be at the quay 90 minutes before all-aboard, or 120 if you went to Nice or Monaco.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on the coast-road bus to get back.
commonMistakes.fix: Bus 600 and bus 15 are slowed by traffic on cruise days. Use the train for the return and keep the bus as a backup.

commonMistakes.mistake: Underestimating the walk from the station.
commonMistakes.fix: The 10-minute route from Villefranche station to the quay has stairs and a climb. Allow for it with bags or a pushchair.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Cocteau chapel on a Monday or Tuesday.
commonMistakes.fix: It opens Wednesday to Sunday only and closes at lunchtime and from mid-November to mid-December.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to fit Èze, Monaco and Nice into one day by bus.
commonMistakes.fix: Pick one or two, or take a ship tour for Èze.

safety: Villefranche itself is small and calm. In Nice, Monaco and on trains and at stations, the UK Foreign Office warns that pickpockets work in gangs, with one distracting you while another goes into your bag. Carry your bag across your body, keep cards and passport apart, and stay alert around tourist sights and cash machines. The lanes in the old town are steep and stepped, and the walk to the station has stairs.
scams: Distraction thefts by pickpocket teams on trains, at stations and around tourist sights, where one person distracts you while another takes from your bag.
accessibility: Tender transfers depend on sea state, and wheelchair users should check with the ship whether tenders can take them on the day. The harbour front is fairly level, but the old town is built on a slope with steps and steep lanes, the walk to the station includes stairs, and Èze is reached by steps. Taxis wait at the tender terminal.
rainyDay: See the Cocteau chapel and the Volti museum in the citadel, then take the train to Nice or Monaco, which have more indoor options. Rough seas can delay or stop tenders, so stay close to the quay if the weather turns.
crowdTips: Villefranche receives more than 200,000 cruise passengers a year and the old town can be busy several times a week from April to October. Since the prefectoral order of 9 December 2025, only one ship of more than 1,300 passengers may call per day and summer calls are capped at 15 a month in July and August. Go ashore early, and use the train rather than the coast-road bus on busy days.

faqs.a: Yes. Ships anchor in the bay and tenders, about 10–15 minutes each way, land at Port de la Santé below the citadel.

faqs.q: Is Villefranche walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The old town is a few minutes from the tender landing, and the station and beach are about 10 minutes on foot, with stairs.

faqs.q: How do I get from Villefranche cruise port to Nice?
faqs.a: Walk about 10 minutes to Villefranche station and take the train, 7–10 minutes to Nice-Ville. Bus 15 from the Octroi stop costs €1.70 (2026) but takes about 25–30 minutes.

faqs.q: How do I get from Villefranche to Monaco?
faqs.a: Take the train from Villefranche station, about 15–20 minutes to Monaco–Monte-Carlo, or bus 600 from the Octroi stop for €2.10 by contactless card (2026).

faqs.q: Can I visit Èze from Villefranche on my own?
faqs.a: Yes, but bus connections are awkward: bus 83 runs from Beaulieu-sur-Mer via Èze-sur-Mer station, and lines 82 and 602 run from Nice. A taxi or ship tour is simpler on a short call.

faqs.q: What can I do in Villefranche in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk the citadel, the Rue Obscure and the Cocteau chapel in the morning, then take the train to Nice or Monaco for the afternoon.
The Plage des Marinières is about 10 minutes' walk from the tender quay, with a shallow drop-off and gravelly sand.
Yes. Watch for pickpockets on trains and in Nice and Monaco, and allow time for the tender queue on your return.
